chunks: Muhammad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, from Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from one who narrated it to him, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
There is neither compulsion nor delegation, but rather a matter between two matters.

He said: I said, 'And what is a matter between two matters?' He said: 'Its likeness is that of a man whom you see committing an act of disobedience, so you forbid him, but he does not desist. Then you leave him, and he commits that act of disobedience. It is not the case that, when he did not accept from you and you left him, you were the one who commanded him to commit the disobedience.'

key_terms.أَمَرْتَهُ: you commanded him; here used to negate that mere non-interference equals ordering the sin
key_terms.أَمْرٌ بَيْنَ أَمْرَيْنِ: a middle reality between compulsion and delegation regarding human acts
key_terms.تَفْوِيضَ: delegation; the belief that actions are fully handed over to humans independently
key_terms.جَبْرَ: compulsion; the belief that a person is forced in his actions without real choice
key_terms.فَنَهَيْتَهُ: you forbade him; you told him not to do the sinful act
key_terms.مَعْصِيَةٍ: an act of disobedience or sin against Allah

ai.seo_question: What does 'neither compulsion nor delegation, but a matter between two matters' mean in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms the Shia creedal principle that human action is neither absolute compulsion nor complete independent delegation from Allah, but a reality between the two. The Imam عليه السلام explains this through an example showing that allowing someone to act after warning him does not mean causing or commanding his sin.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from the one who narrated it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is neither Compulsion nor Delegation, but there is a matter between the two matters’.

I said, ‘And what is the matter between the two matters?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘An example of that is a man you see upon disobedience. So you forbid him, so he does not finish it. So you neglect him (for a while). Then he commits that very disobedience. Therefore it isn’t so when he did not accept from you, so you neglected him, you came to be the one who instructed him with the disobedience’.
